Ravi Desai: quick heads-up 1: noticed short-seq p99 jump ~72ms -> 95ms after yesterday's kernel-packing change.
Elena Park: which change exactly?
Ravi Desai: packer now aggregates up to 12 requests into one kernel call (pack_limit=12) to reduce kernel overhead.
Nina Ortiz: any perf data?
Ravi Desai: perf top snippet: parse_frame 31%, writev_flush 23%, kv_cache_lookup 10%, tokenize_short 9%. writev syscalls doubled.
Theo Kim: streaming chunker config?
Ravi Desai: adaptive-slice min dropped to 128B which increased fragment count for short payloads. combo = lots of tiny writev bursts + higher KV churn.
Elena Park: kv metrics?
Ravi Desai: hitrate fell 0.87 -> 0.70; hot-shard evictions up ~3x.
Nina Ortiz: quick mitigations to try: A) rollback pack_limit=4; B) keep pack high but set min_chunk=512 + enable writev_coalesce.
perf-bot: canary results (10% each, 20m): A -> p99 -9ms, writev -18%, kv_evictions -30%. B -> p99 -16ms, writev -57%, kv_evictions -64%.
Theo Kim: B best for tail but check first-chunk streaming p99 (+5ms). acceptable?
Elena Park: add rollout guard: only enable high-packing when host.writev_rate<400 and kv.hitrate>0.82. also add kernel->batcher shard_affinity hint.
Ravi Desai: implemented guard + metrics (writev_coalesce_hits, avg_iovec, kv_hot_evictions, pack_hist). staging rollout tomorrow. TL;DR: kernel packing gains CPU efficiency but exposed host IO/KV bottlenecks; fix = coalesce + chunk sizing + affinity guard. :white_check_mark:
